title.narrative: Sverige-Ukraina Partnerskap för en Modern och Effektiv Skattemyndighet 2020-2023
Swedish-Ukrainian Partnership for Modern and Efficient Tax Service 2020-2023

description.narrative: The overall objective for the project is to improve the tax administration capacity and contribute to a transformation of the STS into a more modern, trustworthy, effective and service-oriented tax administration. The overall impacts pursued by the project will be:- increase in the level of tax revenues;- improvement of working environment and conditions;- ensuring the principles of efficiency, equity, fairness and integrity in the service of taxpayers;- strengthen the development of HR services;- modern leaders as role models with value founding and sustainable leadership;- employees with responsibility and capability of self-development. Component 1, Leadership and Co-workership: Target: A corporate culture supporting the understanding of the mission & vision of STS in order to increase both individual and corporate motivation for transition to the new STS. Outcome: Improved tax administration capacity and contribution to a transformation of the STS into a more modern, trustworthy, effective and service-oriented tax administration. Component 2, Taxpayer Oriented Approach: Target: More taxpayer oriented communication and services (digital and others). Outcome: Services and other interaction meet taxpayer needs and strengthen trust for STS.

Achievements reported for 2021 include the following.
The programme has implemented activities in the areas of Leadership and Co-workership (LCW) and Taxpayer Oriented Approach (TOA). A large amount activities have been carried out to improve the tax administration capacity and contribute to a transformation of the local Tax Authority STS into a more modern, trustworthy, effective and service-oriented tax administration. STA (the Swedish Tax Authority) have worked to support STS in the development of a solid and constantly ongoing training process for a long-term enhancement of both leadership and co-workership. These activities are reported in different clusters such as Change Management (CM), Internal Communication and Leadership.
A Result Matrix has been produced for the project, showing planned activities in progress. However, the activities during the year have appeared to happen at an ad hoc basis. STA concludes that they are linked and relevant to the STS development strategies but also that STS need to follow a more systemic approach.
A Risk Mitigation Matrix has been produced for the project, and includes; Organisational risks, Project management risks, Environmental risks and External risks. In the 2021 progress report, STA also submits comments and some observations regarding Organisational Risks and Project Management Risks (chapter 9.1).
Progress during 2022 has been very limited. After the Russian full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, STA have struggled unsuccessfully to engage STS in programme implementation. This development has called into question the ownership of STS, while it remains uncertain whether it is the contents of the current programme which has been deemed irrelevant by STS, if the programme framework has not been sufficiently adaptive to contextual changes in its design, or if the challenges boil down to STS assessment of STA capacity, to individual relationships or to circumstances beyond reasonable reach for STA. STA has implied that other donor funded programmes in the tax area supply direct implementation capacity (handout of technical assistance) which might appear more attractive than twinning style partnerships between fellow authorities of the nature STA represents. Only around half of the funds budgeted for the programme have been utilized.
Details on progress during 2022 will be described in the next progress report which is expected from STA in early 2023.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
